newsitem.title: USA: Panel urges Perot be out of presidential debates.
newsitem.headline: Panel urges Perot be out of presidential debates.

text.p: A bipartisan commission planning for the U.S. presidential debates will recommend that third-party candiate Ross Perot be excluded from the debates between President Bill Clinton and Republican Bob Dole, NBC and CNN reported on Tuesday.

A spokesman for the Commission on Presidential Debates would neither confirm nor deny the reports by the two U.S. television networks but said it would announce its recommendations on the conduct of the 1996 debates at noon in Washington (1600 GMT).

NBC and CNN quoted unidentified sources with knowledge of the commission's deliberations as saying Perot, who participated in the 1992 debates and won about 19 percent of the popular vote that year, be excluded this time around.

This year, however, the Texas billionaire has been garnering only single-digit support as head of the newly created Reform Party dedicated to a balanced federal budget, opposition to free trade and campaign finance reform.

The commission, chaired by former chairmen of the Republican and Democratic parties, was formed in an attempt to take organization of the debates -- crucial to U.S. presidential election contests -- out of the partisan arena. Its decisions are not binding, however, and would need to be agreed to by the Clinton and Dole campaigns.

The decision to exclude Perot, a star of the 1992 debates, would surely stir widespread controversy. The Dole camp had opposed his inclusion, fearing he would likely take more votes away from their struggling candidate than from the front-running Clinton, while the president's team had said it welcome Perot into the debates.
